title: Analysis code and aggregate results: Nurse-Charted Congestion–Perfusion Phenotypes in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Perfusion Replicates, Congestion Is Documentation-Dependent
description:
Cohort-definition and analysis code, together with all aggregate outputs, for a study that defined and externally replicated a bedside congestion–perfusion phenotype in the cardiac intensive care unit.

The phenotype combines the two signs critical care nurses chart most often: pitting-oedema depth (ordinal 0–5) and capillary refill time (>3 s). It was developed in 20,806 first cardiac intensive care unit stays in MIMIC-IV v3.1 (12,052 stays with both signs documented; 758 in-hospital deaths) and replicated in the eICU Collaborative Research Database v2.0 (1,541 stays; 152 in-hospital deaths).

Headline results: adding the phenotype to 23 routinely available variables raised the AUROC from 0.858 to 0.871; the increment was carried predominantly by the perfusion axis (impaired perfusion alone +0.0101 versus +0.0038 for congestion). Only the perfusion axis transported to the second database (mortality 6.24% versus 33.96% for adequate versus impaired perfusion; transferred-model AUROC 0.835; observed-to-expected ratio 0.92). The nurse-charted congestion measurement is absent from eICU-CRD, alternative congestion definitions added no incremental discrimination, and the congestion component is therefore documentation-dependent rather than transportable.

No row-level patient data are included. The PhysioNet data use agreements for both databases prohibit redistribution of patient-level records; only aggregate tables and the analysis code are provided.
